title: Geometrically connected fibres of proper maps to normal schemes
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that $S$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point], and normal: every local ring of $S$ is an integrally closed domain. Assume that $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], that every generic point of an irreducible component of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] maps to $\xi$, and that the structure map induces $H^0(X_\xi,\mathcal O_{X_\xi})=\kappa(\xi)$ as $\kappa(\xi)$-algebras [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Then the canonical map $\mathcal O_S\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ is an isomorphism and every fibre of $f$ is geometrically connected: for every $s\in S$ and every field extension $L/\kappa(s)$, the scheme $X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}L$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. No Noetherian or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, label lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal, all six hypotheses and both conclusions.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$. It contains $\xi$, since $\overline{\{\xi\}}=S$. Put $Y=f^{-1}U$ and $K=\kappa(\xi)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), $g:Y\to U$ is proper, hence finite type and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. It is reduced, its local rings being those of $X$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], $A$ is a domain; it has fraction field $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](2): the generic stalk is a field and hence equals its residue field. Also $Y_\xi=X_\xi$.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, label lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal, proof; affine Stein-factorization assembly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine] to $g$: with $B=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ it gives $Y\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{\pi}U$, where $A\to B$ is integral and $q$ has geometrically connected fibres. By [lem-trf-reduced-dominant-generic-restriction] applied to the original $f$ and the quasi-compact open $V=Y$, restriction $B\to\Gamma(Y_\xi,\mathcal O)$ is injective. With $\alpha:K\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X_\xi,\mathcal O)$ the hypothesis isomorphism, $r=\alpha^{-1}\circ\mathrm{res}:B\hookrightarrow K$ sends the image of $a\in A$ to $a/1$.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, label lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal, proof; affine Stein-factorization assembly.

proof.text: Via $r$, $B$ is a subring of $K$ containing $A$, so $B$ is a domain and $A\to B$ is injective. The induced $\operatorname{Frac}(B)\to K$, $b/c\mapsto r(b)/r(c)$ ($c\ne0$), is injective, and surjective as $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. As $A\to B$ is injective, $(0)_B$ lies over $(0)_A$, so [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](2) identifies both schemes as integral and the generic-stalk map as this function-field isomorphism. The map $\pi$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: for affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq U$, $\pi^{-1}W=W\times_U\operatorname{Spec}B\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_AB)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction], integral over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change]. Local rings of $U$ are those of $S$, hence normal. Therefore [lem-trf-integral-birational-normal-isomorphism] makes $\pi$ an isomorphism. Then [def-weil-affine-spectrum] makes the canonical $A\to B$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, label lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal, proof; affine Stein-factorization assembly.

proof.text: The canonical sheaf map is thus an isomorphism over every nonempty affine open; on the empty open both rings are zero. Its inverse maps commute with restriction by uniqueness. On an arbitrary open, restrict a section to an affine cover and apply these inverses. Agreement on overlaps is checked on affine subopens using injectivity there, so the sheaf axiom glues them uniquely. This is an inverse to $\mathcal O_S\to f_*\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Tag 0AY8, label lemma-geometrically-connected-fibres-towards-normal, proof; affine Stein-factorization assembly.

proof.text: For $s\in S$ and a field extension $L/\kappa(s)$ choose $U$ containing $s$. Since $g=\pi q$ and $\pi$ is an isomorphism, the defining fibre products [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identify $X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}L$ with the fibre of $q$ over the corresponding field-valued point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. It is nonempty and connected by [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine](iii).
